input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Nodes: all seven whiteboard entities are kept as-is (ECS hosting Kong, Lambda x25, RDS PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, SNS, Non-Production account, Production account). The Lambda icon is one logical unit, so it stays a single node. The 'Service Teams' human actors are pruned; the non-production account is the system entry point. SQS is mentioned once in the audio for the deployment notification, but it is not drawn on the whiteboard and its endpoints are not clearly stated, so it is not added as a node. 2) Ledger: visual_connections has 7 entries; each is emitted once with the same source and target, including both directions of ECS<->Lambda, ECS<->Non-Prod and Lambda<->DynamoDB. 3) Audio-grounded additions (not in the ledger, explicitly stated): RDS -> Lambda (the compliance framework defined in RDS is matched against the build events), Lambda -> SNS (SNS is used for the promotion), and SNS -> Production Environment (the notification triggers Lambda running in the prod account). These connect the otherwise orphan RDS and SNS nodes. 4) Flows: flow 0 = build event capture (Non-Prod -> Kong on ECS -> Lambda -> DynamoDB); flow 1 = promote request and compliance assessment (DynamoDB and RDS read by Lambda, pass/fail result back through ECS to Non-Prod); flow 2 = promotion and deployment (Lambda -> SNS -> Prod, artifacts copied Non-Prod -> Prod). The direction and purpose of the two return edges (Lambda -> ECS, ECS -> Non-Prod) are inferred as the API response path, since the audio does not describe them directly. 5) Self-check: visual_connections entries = 7; edges emitted = 10 (7 ledger + 3 audio-grounded). 10 >= 7.

graph.name: National Australia Bank: Deputy Compliance Platform for Automated Cloud Deployment Promotion
graph.notes: NAB's Deputy platform is an API-based solution that automates compliance attestation for service teams moving thousands of workloads to AWS. Build events from team pipelines in non-production accounts are captured through Kong on ECS and Lambda into DynamoDB. On a promote call, Lambda assesses those events against the compliance framework (standards and controls) held in RDS PostgreSQL, with a pass or fail result. On success, SNS notifies the production account to trigger the promotion and artifacts are copied from non-prod to prod. Designed for 80 to 100 NAB service teams.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Runs Kong, which publishes the Deputy API endpoints. Receives pipeline build events and promote/deploy API calls from the service teams' non-production accounts.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: About 25 Lambda functions (x25 on the whiteboard). Captures build events and stores them in DynamoDB, and executes the compliance assessment by matching build events against the standards and controls in RDS. Result is success or failure. Chosen for speed to market, no infrastructure to manage and low operational overhead.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: RDS PostgreSQL. Holds the compliance framework (standard, control, how it is tested), plus which teams exist and which services they run. Chosen because this data is relational.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores build events and their evidence from team pipelines (e.g. build started, code scan executed) as key-value pairs. Chosen for low operational overhead and performance.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Used for promotion. Securely sends notifications to production accounts that the platform team has no access to, and fans out to 80 to 100 NAB service teams.

nodes.name: Non Production Environment
nodes.notes: Service team's non-production account, where their pipelines run. Sends build events and makes the promote and deploy API calls to Deputy.

nodes.name: Production Environment
nodes.notes: Service team's production account. Runs distributed Deputy components (Lambda in prod) that are triggered for promotion. Receives the promoted artifacts and the deployment trigger.

edges.notes: Pipelines in the non-production account send all build events to Kong running on ECS. Promote and deploy API calls use the same entry point.
Kong forwards the events and API calls to Lambda.
Lambda captures the build events and stores them in DynamoDB.
On a promote call, Lambda reads the team's stored build events from DynamoDB.
Lambda reads the compliance standards and controls from RDS PostgreSQL to match against the build events.
Assessment result (success or failure) returned to the Kong API layer. Purpose inferred; the audio does not describe this arrow.
API response with the compliance result returned to the non-production account. Purpose inferred; the audio does not describe this arrow.
When compliance passes and promotion is requested, a notification is published to SNS.
SNS notifies the production account and triggers the promotion there (Lambda running in prod). Fan-out to many team accounts.
Artifacts are copied from the non-production account to the production account. A deployment message (SQS in the audio) then triggers the team's deployment tools.
